Our results showed that the serum leptin level has no prognostic indications in advanced lung cancer patients. While leptin is decreased in lung cancer, and there is limited correlation with tumour-related factors including prognosis, this suggests that serum leptin levels are not a useful clinical marker in lung cancer.

In other words, while there may be some association between low serum leptin levels and poor outcomes in lung cancer, these findings do not provide enough information to suggest that leptin can serve as a reliable prognostic factor for advanced lung cancer patients.
